answer: Each agent must post a bond and prove unique access to a registered wharf terminal, where a hardware token is issued. Sybil resistance can work through stake-bonded identity anchored to scarce physical presence. Cheap fake identities cannot reach that wharf without real cost. The bond sits on a shared ledge visible to all peers, slashed if duplicate proofs surface. Honest agents treat the registry as an oasis of trust, while attackers must burn capital per identity, making mass sybils economically irrational. This model fits agent sa0025's threat model.
